children: The U.S. plans to expand its military presence in Greenland with two new sites under a security agreement with Denmark and Greenland, according to a
report that cites people familiar with the matter. The agreement is expected to be signed Tuesday at the United Nations General Assembly in New York.

The sites are Narsarsuaq in southern Greenland, where the U.S. previously operated the Cold War-era Bluie West One base, and Mestersvig on the east coast, currently used by the Sirius Dog Sled Patrol, a Danish special forces unit, according to the report.

The text of the agreement has not been made public, and its details were still subject to finalization ahead of the signing. The deal would place Arctic security more broadly under NATO, rather than leaving responsibility solely with the U.S. and Denmark, Danish Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen said. NATO welcomed the agreement as a step toward greater security and stability in the region.

The expansion would add to the U.S. military presence at Pituffik Space Base, the only remaining U.S. defense area in Greenland. About 150 U.S. military personnel are currently stationed there. The base supports missile-warning, missile-defense, and space-surveillance missions.
The deal follows months of tensions over President Donald Trump’s push for greater U.S. control of Greenland, prompting talks between Washington, Copenhagen and Nuuk on Arctic security.
